# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 39 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 39 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_039_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Part 1 — Two Angels, Two Ways

**39:1** "In the first commandment," the Shepherd said, "I told you to keep faith, fear, and self-control." "Yes, I remember, lord," I said. "Now," he continued, "I want to explain the power behind these commandments — what each one does and why it matters."

**39:2** "Every person has two angels accompanying them," he said, "one representing righteousness and one representing wickedness." "But how will I know which one is at work in me," I asked, "since both are present with me?"

**39:3** "Listen carefully," he said. "The angel of righteousness is gentle, humble, quiet, and calm. Whenever he rises up in your heart, he speaks to you immediately about what is right — about purity, holiness, self-control, every just action, every magnificent virtue. Whenever these things well up in your heart, you can be sure the angel of righteousness is at work in you. That is his character. Trust him and follow his promptings."

**39:4** "Now consider the angel of wickedness. He is hot-tempered, bitter, and foolish, and everything he does tears down God's people. When he stirs up your heart, you can recognize him by what he produces."

**39:5** "But how exactly will I know him, lord?" I asked. "Here is how," he said. "When a burst of anger or bitterness wells up in you — that is him. Also a craving for too many transactions, a taste for excessive food and heavy drinking, a love of unnecessary pleasures, lust for women, greed, arrogance, boasting — everything of that sort. When those impulses rise up in you, you know the angel of wickedness is present."

**39:6** "Now that you know what he produces, stay away from him and don't trust him at all — his work is destructive for God's servants. There you have it: the signatures of both angels. Learn to recognize them, and keep trusting the angel of righteousness."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the moral urgency of Hermas's ethical vision.*
